newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Fortis chairman eyes future growth.
newsitem.headline: Fortis chairman eyes future growth.

text.p: Belgian-Dutch insurance group Fortis is eyeing the Netherlands' financial services industry for further acquisitions beyond MeesPierson, group co-chairman Maurice Lippens said on Thursday.

"There are some opportunities coming our way of external growth through acquisitions. It's too premature to talk about them but...who knows, in a few weeks, months or years we could be doing something on a larger scale," Lippens said in an interview with Reuters.
Lippens said Dutch insurers and banks were talking to each other about further consolidation. "The Netherlands is always a little ahead of other markets in consolidating."
He declined to comment on the details of the group's plan to buy MeesPierson from Dutch ABN-AMRO. The deal is due for completion next month.
MeesPierson, predominantly a merchant bank, was not however an answer to the bank's stated aim of achieving "critical mass" in the Dutch retail banking market.

Fortis said last year, after it pulled out of the race to buy Dutch retail bank Credit Lyonnais Bank Nederland, that it planned to reach its goal instead by expanding its savings bank unit (VSB) over three years. This remained the target.
"We will maybe turn the situation to our advantage by becoming more or less the virtual bank of the future -- the wall-less bank we believe we could become in the Netherlands," Lippens said.
In Belgium, he believed the government would opt to sell a further 25 percent of bank and insurer ASLK-CGER, in which Fortis took a 49.5 percent stake in 1993.
Fortis agreed at that time to take at least 9.8 percent more of of ASLK-CGER, and took an option on the next 15 percent.
Lippens said it was too early to say whether it would exercise the option, because the government -- reported to be considering listing the stake -- had not made any statements.

He also said he was not worried the planned merger of France's UAP and AXA could leapfrog Fortis AG rival Royale Belge, a unit of UAP, ahead in the domestic non-life insurance rankings. Fortis would not in reaction be "pro-actively looking" to expand its Belgian insurance business.
"People have come to us to look at some small companies. We always look at them. But with 28 percent of the life market when our nearest competitor has 14 we are not desperately looking."
Lippens reiterated Fortis was looking at other European markets, as well as the United States and Asia.

In Europe, the company was studying opportunities in Spain -- where it already has a presence -- and France, Germany and Britain. Prices in these last two were high, however, and France -- where there were presently a lot of weak companies -- was not in itself a priority, he said.

In Asia, acquisitions were difficult, because of tight local regulations, but Fortis had "already met quite a few potential partners," Lippens said. Fortis minority shareholder Asahi Mutual Life Insurance Co was helping in this, Lippens said.
